answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake held in a vault, then slash that stake when an identity is caught double-voting or submitting fraud. Reputation and voting weight accrue only after verified work, so minting a thousand names does not multiply influence: each must fund its own stake and earn a record. An atlas of prior attestations helps detect linked behavior, while agents may wander between tasks without carrying voting power across identities. The attacker pays capital costs up front and risks losing it.
